extracted.intended_audience: general readers interested in conspiracy theories, media ethics, and modern Swedish media history
extracted.subtask_short: encyclopedic entry on a conspiracy theory
extracted.subtask_description: A Wikipedia-style encyclopedic article documenting the claims, alleged content, responses, sourcing, and media-ethics context of a specific conspiracy theory (Lilla Saltsjöbadsavtalet).

rubrics_metrics.name: Confirmation by independent sources
rubrics_metrics.description: "The alleged agreement, and the meeting at which it should have been prepared, has not been confirmed by independent sources."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Claims about events should be corroborated by independent, reliable sources; absence of independent confirmation weakens the claim. The page cites a TV follow-up (Striptease) that found no evidence for the alleged event.

rubrics_metrics.name: Require reliable sourcing / citations
rubrics_metrics.description: The article flags statements with markers such as "[non-primary source needed]" and "[citation needed]" indicating a need for proper sourcing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assertions—especially extraordinary claims—must be supported by primary or reputable secondary sources. Unsourced or poorly sourced claims should be treated skeptically and are appropriate for tagging or removal until verified.

rubrics_metrics.name: Corroboration via primary records (example: hotel bookings)
rubrics_metrics.description: Investigative follow-up included visiting the hotel where the conference should have taken place and checking booking records (Striptease found no booking related to the alleged event).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where possible, verify alleged meetings or events against primary records (hotel bookings, minutes, sign-in sheets). Direct documentary evidence provides stronger confirmation than hearsay.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eyewitness/participant testimony must be contextualized and corroborated
rubrics_metrics.description: Some journalists (Popova, Gür) confirmed attending a conference in the late 1980s but denied that any agreement had been established; dates and places reported vary (1987 vs 1988/1989).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Participant testimony can confirm that meetings occurred but does not by itself prove contested claims (e.g., that a binding agreement was made). Testimony should be checked for consistency, corroborated by other sources, and interpreted in context.

rubrics_metrics.name: Investigative journalism can reveal fabrication or 'bluff'
rubrics_metrics.description: Journalistic investigative work (e.g., Janne Josefsson's Striptease) is cited as having revealed that the supposed agreement was a "bluff".
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Thorough investigative reporting—interviews, document checks, on-site follow-ups—can be used to refute fabricated claims. Such reporting should be cited when assessing the veracity of conspiratorial narratives.

rubrics_metrics.name: Watch for partisan or extremist amplification
rubrics_metrics.description: "A large group of right-wing extremists market the myth as the great conspiracy within Swedish mass media..."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When a claim is primarily propagated within partisan or extremist circles, treat it with caution; consider the motives and networks amplifying the claim and seek independent verification from neutral sources.

rubrics_metrics.name: Present plausible alternative explanations and acknowledge uncertainty
rubrics_metrics.description: An editor suggested the myth possibly originated from an internal editorial meeting at Dagens Nyheter rather than the alleged Saltsjöbaden conference.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When definitive proof is lacking, document plausible origins or alternative explanations and explicitly acknowledge uncertainty instead of presenting unverified narratives as fact.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adhere to newsroom ethics regarding emphasis on ethnic origin (Press Cooperation Board §10)
rubrics_metrics.description: "Do not emphasize the person's ethnic origin, gender, nationality, occupation, political affiliation, religious beliefs or sexual orientation if it is irrelevant in this context and is discrediting." (Ethical rules for press, television and radio, Pressens Samarbetsnämnd, §10)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reporting should avoid highlighting irrelevant personal attributes (including ethnic origin) that would discredit a person. This is presented as an established ethical standard governing how journalists handle identity details in coverage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use (and critique) visual anonymization practices appropriately (white pixelization / vitpixling)
rubrics_metrics.description: Expressen had used "white pixelization (vitpixling)"—digitally whitening a perpetrator's skin color—to avoid "unnecessary identification" but later described this policy as a "mistake."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Visual anonymization techniques may be used to protect identity or avoid irrelevant emphasis on ethnicity, but newsrooms should review such practices for ethical and editorial appropriateness and be prepared to revise policies that prove problematic.
